Description: Urban Sprawl index for Census Tracts (within CMA's) for Canada in 2016.
Variable Description: A summary measure of urban sprawl ranging theoretically between -3 and +3. This variable is a z-score of the combination of 9 different indicators.
Units: Unitless. Theoretical range from -3 to +3. A standard normal distribution. Higher values mean less urban sprawl.

Description: Number of dwellings in need or repair at the DA level based on the 25% sample of the census.
Variable Description: The proportion of dwellings in need of repair at the dissemination area level in Canada.
Units: Proportion. Range 0 to 1. Higher values mean more dwellings in need of repair.

Description: Average annual air quality at the DA level between 2012 and 2014 for two metrics, PM2.5 and Carbon Monoxide.
Variable Description: Annual Mean MOPITT CO (carbon monoxide) Surface Concentration (2012-2014) in ppb
Units: Parts Per Billion. Range 109.5 to 289.1. Higher values mean more carbon monoxide)

Description: Average annual air quality at the DA level between 2012 and 2014 for two metrics, PM2.5 and Carbon Monoxide.
Variable Description: Annual Mean Satellite-derived PM2.5 (fine particulates) Surface Concentration (2012-2014) in ug/m3
Units: Micrograms per Cubic Meter. Range 0.72 to 13.3. Higher values mean more PM2.5.

Description: Gentrification measure developed by Steinmetz-Wood (https://doi.org/10.1186/s12942-017-0096-6) at the
Variable Description: Gentrified census tract according to Steinmetz-Wood in 2016.

Description: Modified Retail Food Environment Index - Canada 1km (https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/13-20-0001/132000012022001-eng.htm)
Variable Description: The modified Retail Food Environment Index (mRFEI) calculates the proportion of food outlets that sell a wide selection of fresh and nutritious food that operate within each buffer
Units: Categorical. Range 0 to 4. with 4 being the most healthy food stores and 0 being the least.

Description: Annual estimates of average normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and green/grey classification. "Urban greenness" is a measure that assesses the condition and health of an urban landscape. Vegetation contributes to more livable, beautiful communities by helping to clean the air, moderate the local climate, control water flow and provide habitats for wildlife.
Variable Description: Annual average NDVI. AVHRR series satellites were used to generate 1 km, NDVI composites based on surface reflectance data, annually producing 36 composites every 10-days for all of Canada. Resulting cloud free NDVI  composites.
Units: Range between 0-1. Higher values mean more greeness.

Description: The Canadian Active Living Environments (Can-ALE) database is a geographic-based set of measures that represents the active living friendliness of Canadian communities.
Variable Description: Three measures were produced for all DAs in Canada (intersection density, dwelling density, and points of interest), and one measure was produced for all DAs within Census Metropolitan Areas (CMAs) in Canada (transit stops). The can_ale variable is a combined z-score of the three variables.
Units: Combined z-scores of the three variables. Range between -2.1 to +43.8. Higer values mean more active living friendly environments.

Description: Tree canopy is defined as area of vegetation (including leaves, stems, branches, etc.) of woody plants above 5m in height. The dataset developers derived tree canopy cover estimates from the Global Forest Cover Change (GFCC) Surface Reflectance product (GFCC30SR), which is based on enhanced Global Land Survey (GLS) datasets.
Variable Description: Estimated percent of pixel covered by vegetation greater than 5m in height
Units: Average pixels within a DA that are covered by trees. Range 0 to 78. A higher value means more pixels are covered by trees.

Description: Flood Susceptibility Index (FSI) dataset from Natural Resources Canada. This national map of flood susceptibility or flood prone areas is based on patterns of historic flood events as predicted by an ensemble machine learning model. The native resolution of the FSI datasets is 30 m.
Variable Description: Average flood risk over 3 years in a 500m radious around the DA centroid.
Units: Values close to 0 indicate low susceptibility to flooding and values close to 100 indicate areas that are the most susceptible to flooding. Range 2 to 98.

Description: Annual estimates of maximum mean warm-season land surface temperature (LST) recorded by LandSat 8 at 30m resolution. Calculated using Google Earth Engine and public algorithm avaiable here (https://canuedata.ca/docs/LST_GEE-code.docx).
Variable Description: Average land surface temperature over 3 years in a 500m radious around the DA centroid.
Units: Values are in degrees Celcius and range from 3.3 to 37.5.
